title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a set of notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The relevant 4-element sets are the four 2-torsion points, or equivalently the four branch points of E → P^1. Such a set is a torsor under E[2] ≅ F_2^2. This page is a preliminary 'dictionary' section on 4-element sets.

(1) It ends the identification begun on the previous page. Let V ⊂ S_I be the Klein four-group, whose translations make I an affine plane over F_2. Set J = V^*, the three lines of V. The map from the 6 two-element subsets (= the 6 affine lines of I) to the 3 partitions of type (2,2) sends A ↦ {A, I∖A}. It is identified with the map sending an affine line to its direction, a vector line D ⊂ V. The fibre over a partition j consists of its two blocks. These blocks are exactly the points of the affine quotient line I/D_j.

(2) The forgetful functor Aff_2(F_2) → (Ens_4) is an equivalence. Here the source is affine planes over F_2 with affine isomorphisms and the target is 4-element sets with bijections. Interlinear remark: one may define an affine F_2-plane structure on I as a structure on I alone, e.g. a subgroup of S_I; this structure is canonical. The marginal note seems to say the same in the language of affine varieties/finite sets.

(3) Claim: the functor (Ens_4) → (Gr), I ↦ S_I, is fully faithful on groupoids. Equivalently, S_4 is a complete group: trivial centre and Aut = Inn. He remarks it suffices to check this for S_4.

(4) Proof strategy: build a quasi-inverse on the essential image (Gr)' of groups isomorphic to S_4. For such G, take I_G = the set of Sylow 3-subgroups; there are exactly four. On the next page he shows this is canonically a V-torsor:
- V is the maximal abelian normal subgroup.
- I_G is the set of splittings of 1 → V → G^+ → A_3 → 1.
- V acts on these splittings by inner automorphisms; the action is free because V^{A_3} = 0, and transitive by Schur–Zassenhaus/conjugacy.
- For G = S_I the bijection is i ↦ the Sylow 3-subgroup fixing i.

The overall purpose is to set up canonical, functorial (groupoid-level) identifications. These later let level-2 structures, S_3 = GL_2(F_2) acting via the cross-ratio/λ-line, and the anabelian-style 'recover the set from its group' be handled stack-theoretically.
errors: The equivalence Aff_2(F_2) ≃ (Ens_4) and the full faithfulness of I ↦ S_I only hold for groupoids (isomorphisms only). Arbitrary maps of 4-sets are not affine, and S_I is only functorial in bijections. Grothendieck clearly intends groupoids but does not say so on this page.
The hesitation over whether it suffices to state completeness for S_4 is harmless: full faithfulness of a functor between connected groupoids reduces to a single object. No real gap.

ideas.what: A 4-element set carries a canonical affine F_2-plane structure (Klein V ⊂ S_4). Lines ↔ 2-subsets, directions ↔ (2,2)-partitions, giving the exact sequence 1→V→S_4→S_3→1.
Forgetful functor Aff_2(F_2) → Ens_4 is an equivalence of groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: AGL_2(F_2) = S_4; equivalence of groupoids of torsor-type structures

ideas.what: I ↦ S_I fully faithful, i.e. S_4 is complete (trivial centre, all automorphisms inner).
Recovering I from G ≅ S_4 as the set of Sylow 3-subgroups, a V-torsor of splittings of 1→V→A_4→A_3→1.
ideas.modern_name: quasi-inverse via Sylow subgroups; torsor of splittings (H^1 vanishing / Schur–Zassenhaus)

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical finite group theory (S_4 = AGL_2(F_2), completeness of S_4, Sylow-3 recovery of the 4-set), written in Grothendieck's functorial groupoid style. It is preparatory material for level-2 structures on elliptic curves; nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'La fibre d'un j ∈ P_1(I)' should read 'j ∈ 𝔓_{2,2}(I)' (a (2,2)-partition), and 'l'espace quotient I/D_j'.
Group symbols written 𝔊_I in the machine transcription are 𝔖_I (symmetric group).
'Le foncteur "ensemble [?] de la structure"' is likely 'ensemble sous-jacent à la structure'; the target is 'la cat. des ensembles à quatre éléments'.
'[Pourrait-] Est-ce bien sûr de l'énoncer pour 𝔖_4 ?' is better read as '(il suffirait bien sûr de l'énoncer pour 𝔖_4 ?)'.
Marginal note: reading uncertain, possibly 'i.e. variétés affines planes sur F_2 ... ensembles finis'.
